plan.title: AD lesional vs control hallmark pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which hallmark pathways are enriched in the atopic-dermatitis lesional (treated) vs control skin comparison, and the analysis already has a DESeq2 results table (de_results.csv, 12000 genes x 8 columns) for the treated vs control contrast — so no new differential expression model is fitted. The plan (1) profiles sample structure from the raw counts to confirm the treated/control grouping and flag sample_01's low library size as an inherited QC note rather than something the enrichment step must re-derive, (2) runs preranked GSEA (gseapy, Python per the user's constraint) on the delivered DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (the first-pass human collection) with Reactome as the follow-up collection, both staged in the reference store, (3) reports leading-edge genes, the pinned collection versions, the ranking-metric choice, and the method-dependence caveat. All steps run in Python per the explicit user constraint; DESeq2/fgsea R-track defaults from the knowledge base are translated to their Python equivalents (pydeseq2 for the vst-style QC transform, gseapy prerank for fgsea-preranked GSEA) since only Python tooling is permitted.

input.query: gseapy.prerank function parameters rnk gmt seed permutation_num min_size max_size
gseapy python gene set enrichment prerank
gseapy Python gene set enrichment analysis

steps.method: DESeq2-equivalent sample structure QC via pydeseq2 vst + PCA on raw counts
gseapy prerank GSEA on the Wald statistic (stat column) from delivered DESeq2 results, against MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets
gseapy prerank GSEA on the Wald statistic against Reactome pathway gene sets (human subset)
Enrichment report with leading-edge genes, method-dependence caveat, reproducibility record
